title: Ibovespa Extends Winning Streak
body: The Ibovespa rose 0.3% to close at 175,665 on Friday, reversing earlier losses and extending its winning streak to eight consecutive sessions. Brazil generated 58,568 formal jobs in July, well below market expectations of 112,000 and sharply lower than the 145,161 positions created in June. On the inflation front, the PPI increased 1.94% year-on-year in July, easing from 2.47% in June, while the IGP-M declined. The softer labor market and inflation readings may give the BCB room to maintain its current pace of 25-basis-point rate cuts, lending support to credit-sensitive stocks. Financials advanced, with Bradesco and Itaúsa up 0.9% and Banco do Brasil gaining 1%. Exchange operator B3 climbed 2% after JPMorgan reported that emerging-market equity funds saw higher inflows, with Brazil rebounding following four consecutive weeks of substantial outflows. Utilities also moved higher, led by a 0.9% rise in Axia. Petrobras gained 2% after Bradesco BBI raised its recommendation on the stock to Outperform from Neutral. In contrast, Vale slipped 0.7% after a trial on the taxation of profits generated by the miner's foreign subsidiaries was suspended. title: TSX Falls on Mining and Energy Losses
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index fell 0.8% to close at 36,554 on Friday, pressured by broad weakness in mining and energy stocks. Mining names dropped sharply as gold prices declined after hawkish remarks from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh reinforced expectations for an interest rate hike next month. Agnico Eagle slid 3.8%, Barrick fell 3.1%, WPM lost 2.6%, and Kinross dropped 3.5%. Energy producers also retreated as oil prices weakened following increased traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and an agreement between Iran and Oman on a revenue-sharing framework for the key waterway. Canadian Natural declined 1.3%, Suncor slipped 1.1%, and Imperial Oil was down 1%. AI-infrastructure stocks mirrored losses in U.S. chipmakers, with Shopify down 0.6% and Celestica tumbling 5.5%. Financials and the broader market were more resilient, underpinned by Canada's 3.3% GDP growth in Q2, the strongest expansion in nearly two years. title: US Stocks Fall on Rising Fed Hike Bets
body: US stock indices ended lower on Friday as chipmakers pared the previous session's gains and a more hawkish tone from Fed Chair Warsh bolstered expectations of a rate hike next month. The S&P 500 slipped 0.2%, the Nasdaq lost 0.7%, and the Dow edged down. Marvell dropped 10.3% despite beating earnings forecasts and raising its guidance. The broader chip sector retreated after rallying earlier in the week on Nvidia's strong results; Nvidia fell 4.6%, Broadcom declined 0.7%, and AMD slid 2.3%. Large-cap tech "hyperscalers" largely held their ground, with Alphabet up 1.5%, Microsoft gaining 1.7%, Amazon jumping 4%, and Meta advancing 1.2%. In his remarks at the Jackson Hole Symposium, Warsh said underlying inflation was not easing and pledged to continue fighting price pressures until they converge with the Fed's 2% target. His comments led traders to increase bets on a rate hike next month. Industrial and pharmaceutical names also weakened, with AbbVie down 1% and Lam Research off 5.2%. title: Crude Oil Posts Weekly Loss
body: Crude oil fell to $83.40 a barrel on Friday, extending weekly losses to roughly 4%, as traders increasingly interpreted tensions with Iran as an economic and sanctions-driven dispute rather than an imminent threat to physical supply. The perceived supply risk was further eased by improving tanker flows through the Strait of Hormuz and progress on the proposed Iran–Oman transport corridor. Goldman Sachs estimated that Persian Gulf oil exports have risen to about 15–16 million barrels per day—still well below the pre-conflict range of 22–24 million barrels, but substantially higher than the March trough of roughly 5–6 million barrels per day. In parallel, Iran and Oman agreed on a revenue-sharing framework for the strait, though Tehran stressed this does not signal an immediate reopening. At the same time, the Trump administration has reportedly informed mediators that it does not plan to reinstate the terms of a preliminary agreement reached with Iran in June, which later collapsed.
